    How these figures are built

    Stock count analysis

    The stock Business Central holds at a location at the end of the month (the month's Inventory Valuation: opening, increases, decreases, closing) against the physical count uploaded as the Excel form. Every difference at the average cost of the month end. Business Central is read only.

    Choose the location and the month the count closes.

    By category

    BC closing value, counted value and the differences by item category (Business Central's; the form's when the item is not in BC).

    Lines

    Inventory valuation

    Counts uploaded

    Every count form uploaded for this company, by month and location; a new upload of the same location and month replaces the one before.

    How these figures are built

    BC closing quantity: Inventory by date at the last day of the month for the location (the item card in Business Central).

    Closing value: the remaining cost of the open item ledger entries of the location today (actual and expected cost, in proportion to the quantity still open), less the cost of every entry posted after the month end. The same done for the quantity must give BC's closing quantity: the line Quantity check says whether it does.

    Increases and decreases: the entries of the month (from the 1st to the last day) with a positive and a negative quantity, at their cost. Opening = closing − increases − decreases.

    Average cost at the month end = closing value ÷ closing quantity. When the closing quantity is not above zero: the cost of the month's increases, then the item card's Unit Cost; the column Cost from names it.

    Unit cost (card): the Unit Cost on the item card in Business Central when the analysis is read; Difference × card cost values the same difference at it, beside the value at the average cost of the month end.

    Difference = counted − BC closing quantity; its value = difference × average cost. A blank count is Not counted, never zero. Items with BC stock that are not on the form are listed as Not on the form.

    The figures are exact once the cost adjustment (Adjust Cost – Item Entries) has run up to the month end: in this Business Central it runs by hand (Automatic Cost Adjustment = Never), as part of the month-end close.

    Excel drops the zeros in front of a number: a code like 7020 on the form is matched to the one BC item 007020.

    Posted after the form: the count equals the form's system stock (Gjendje Finance), but BC changed after the form was printed, with documents dated in the month (a transfer or a return dated the last day and posted days later). The documents are named on the line. These lines are kept out of the shortages, surpluses and net difference: the question is the cut-off of those documents, not the count.

    Shrinkage KPIs

    The count differences of a location, month by month and by category, against the waste the category is allowed: what is lost beyond it is the unjustified value. Upload the month's count of a location: the rest (the stock before, the month's ins and outs at their posted cost, the categories) is read from Business Central.

    Categories & waste

    How these figures are built

    Count: the count form uploaded here for the location and month (Kartela, GjendjeFizike; the same file as Stock count analysis). Difference = counted − theoretical, valued at the item's KMSH: the posted cost of its outs in the month, else of its ins, else the item card's Unit Cost. Items with stock not on the form, or left blank, take no difference and are shown apart.

    A month with no form uploaded takes the count posted in Business Central: the item adjustment dated the last day of the month, its document starting with IF (IF 01.10.2026, IFAMB 01/10/2026…), quantity and cost as posted.

    In and out: the month's other entries of the location, by sign (purchases, transfers, consumption by the recipes, sales). Staff consumption, declared waste (FIRO) and corrections that cancel each other are netted per item.

    Opening = stock at the end of the month before; counted = stock at the month end, with the count posted; theoretical = opening + in − out.

    KMSH / Dalje = the cost of the month's outs, as posted. Diferenca / Dalje = loss ÷ KMSH / Dalje. % Delta = difference ÷ out, in quantity.

    Investigate: Diferenca / Dalje above the % Waste of the category. Unjustified (recommended) = loss − % Waste × KMSH / Dalje, never below zero. Unjustified (Excel) = the whole loss of a category marked Investigate, as the KPI workbook counts it.

    Category: from the item card (Item Category Group 4 and 5; Group 2 for PN) through the map in Categories & waste, with exceptions per item. An item the map does not reach (packaging, cleaning, uniforms) takes its card's own group in Business Central (Group 4, else Group 3 or 2), marked "from BC", with no % Waste until one is set.

    Values are exact once the cost adjustment (Adjust Cost – Item Entries) has run for the month.

    How these figures are built

    Menu & food cost

    Which menu items sell a lot and contribute well, and where the price, the recipe or the losses need a look. Items and margins as Menu engineering reads them (Simphony sales less VAT, portion cost from the BC recipes); the food cost trend by week against the P&L month.

    Popularity × profit

    Each dot is a menu item of the period: to the right, more items sold (log scale); up, more margin per item sold (net price less the portion cost). The lines are the median items sold and the average margin per item; the size is the item's total margin; the colour is its food cost against the target.

    Food cost % by week

    Theoretical: what the items sold cost by their recipes, as a share of their net sales, week by week. Actual: the cost of goods of the P&L as a share of its revenue, month by month. The space between the two is what the menu does not explain: waste, portions, staff meals, stock differences or a recipe that is wrong.

    Where to look

    Items above the food cost target of Settings (Menu engineering parameters), the largest margin lost first. Sold more than the median: the price first, since a small rise reaches many sales. Sold less: the recipe and the portion first.

    How these figures are built

    Sales blocked by stock

    The sales Business Central cannot post because a component is short at the location, and the components today's Simphony sales will run out of before they are imported. Read every few minutes; Business Central and Simphony are only read.

    Reading…

    By location

    Click a location to see only its items.

    Blocking the sales now

    Components the open assembly orders need more of than the location holds now: until the stock is there (a receipt, a transfer, a count), the orders that use them, and their sales, are not posted. Below them, the ones Business Central still flags whose stock has come: those orders can be posted. Largest sales held first; click a row for the menu items.

    At risk today

    What Simphony has sold today and Business Central has not imported yet, through the recipes: the components whose stock, after what the open orders already need, does not cover it. Fix them before the import, and the sales post.

    How these figures are built

    The Simphony sales are imported into Business Central as assembly orders, one per menu item, location and day; an order is posted when its components can be taken out of the location's stock.

    Blocking now: need = the remaining quantity of every open assembly line of the component at the location, in its base unit; on hand = its stock at the location now; short = need − on hand, above zero. Business Central's Avail. Warning is set when a line is checked and can stay on after the stock has come: such a component is shown as covered now. Sales held = the portions of the blocked orders × the menu item's price in Simphony.

    At risk today: the menu items sold today in Simphony (current business day) less what is already imported, exploded through their BC recipe (Assembly BOM, units converted). A component is at risk when on hand − the open orders' need − today's need is below zero.

    The Simphony menu item number is the BC item number; each restaurant's Simphony location and BC location come from the location registry (Settings → Location intelligence).

    A profit and loss of every sales channel (Simphony order type: dine in, take away, Wolt, Glovo…), on RHG's Wolt template: net sales, the channel's costs, cost of goods, other variable costs, the contribution, then the result after fixed and shared costs. Sales from Simphony; cost of goods from the recipes in Business Central; the rest from BC accounts or from the parameters. The period is the one chosen above.

    Per channel, the costs that Simphony does not hold. Amounts per month are per location. Where BC accounts are given, the net change of those accounts on the location's department replaces the amount typed here. Nothing is assumed: an empty commission stays at zero and is flagged.

    Where 100 of net sales goes

    Each channel's net sales split into cost of goods, the channel's costs, other variable costs, fixed and shared costs, and what is left; the figure on the right is the result after full costs, as a share of net sales.

    EMC privileges

    Simphony Configuration API: connection

Its password comes by email to the account's address. Type the password here yourself: it stays on the server, the screen only shows whether it is set. The tower only reads (get calls).

    Every Simphony check against the invoice Billy fiscalized for it: whether, with which IIC and FIC and at what time; the tills and units (kiosks included), shifts and operators, the summary invoices, and the sales book in the columns of the law in place of the Self-Care download.

    Any days up to yesterday, 62 at most; the usual view is the last days of Settings.

    Billy: connection & mapping

    The address of Billy Bridge and, per company, its NUIS and the Billy user. Each person types the password here; it stays on the server and the screen only shows whether it is set. The tower only reads: sign-in, sales invoices and invoices.

    Day by day

    Every restaurant together: the checks of each day, fiscalized, fiscalized late, or not fiscalized. Click a day for its restaurants; a case for the records behind it.

    Every check

    Each Simphony check with its invoice: number, IIC, FIC, the time it was fiscalized and how long after the check closed.

    Invoices without a check, and without a FIC

    Fiscalized invoices no Simphony check accounts for (issued by hand, another till, or a check changed after it was fiscalized), and invoices of the bridge that never got a FIC.

    Returns tracking

    Every cancel, return, reopen or change of a Simphony check, and the corrective invoice in Billy that closes it. None: the check is an unfiscalized return. Voids and error corrects before closing are listed with no fiscal effect: nothing had been fiscalized.

    Corrective invoices with no Simphony event

    Corrective or negative invoices in Billy that no cancel, return, reopen or change of a check accounts for: a correction made at the till without Simphony, or of a check outside the days read.

    Every restaurant, every day

    Checks not fiscalized in the square; green when every check has its invoice. Hover for Simphony against fiscalized.

    Tills and business units

    Every till (tcrcode) and business unit (businUnitCode) with invoices in the period, and the restaurant it belongs to: mapped in Settings, or proposed where its invoices match the checks. A till of a restaurant whose invoices match no check, like a kiosk, is shown apart.

    Shift and operator

    Simphony checks by the employee who closed them against the invoices of their operator code, shift by shift. The difference is fiscalized less Simphony.

    Orders

    Documents of Billy with the payment method ORDER: orders, kept apart from the invoices (cash or account) so they are not matched to the checks or put in the sales book. For each order, the invoice that closes it (the invoice names its orders), else whether an invoice of the same total follows on the same till within a day.

    Summary invoices

    Invoices that sum up other invoices (their IIC references): fiscalized or not, and which of the invoices they refer to are found in Billy for the period.

    Sales book

    Every invoice of the period in the columns of the sales book (exempt, without VAT, zero rate and exports, taxable value and VAT by rate), checked against the law; the Excel is the book with the cases.

    How the reconciliation works

    Simphony ↔ BC

    Every restaurant and business day: what Simphony sold, what the POS import brought into Business Central, what was invoiced to the restaurant's customer and what is still open on the invoice. A day that does not meet becomes an exception in the register, with its owner; it closes when the figures meet.

    Day by day

    Every restaurant together: what came into Business Central through the POS import against what Simphony sold (the dashed mark). Click a day for its restaurants; a case below for its days.

    Every restaurant, every day

    A square per day: green when Simphony, the import and the invoice meet; the gap of the import against Simphony in the square. Click a square for the day.

    Menu items and BC items

    Menu items of the period imported with no BC item, with an item BC does not know or has blocked, with an item that needs a recipe and has none, or sold in Simphony and never imported. Each one is an exception for the cost controller.

    Table

    Lags and tolerance

    A day is pending, not an exception, until its lag has passed. A gap counts above the larger of the amount and the percentage.

    How the reconciliation works

    Takings POS ↔ BC

    Every restaurant and business day: what the till took by tender (Simphony) against what Business Central received for it, tender by tender, on the restaurant's department. A day not received after its lag becomes a case in the register.

    Day by day

    Every restaurant and channel together: what the till took, as received in Business Central, still within the lag, or not received after it. Click a day for its restaurants; a case below for its days.

    Every restaurant and channel, every day

    A channel is the tenders that land on the same BC accounts (cash on the cash box, each card on its bank). A square per day: green received, amber received late, red not received after the lag, dashed still within the lag. Click a square for the day.

    ReceivedReceived lateNot receivedWithin the lag

    By restaurant and channel

    Table

    Tips, VAT and service charge

    Net sales in Simphony include VAT; the service charge is apart; the tenders are what guests paid. Tenders − (net sales + service charge) is what was paid on top: card tips keyed on the till, rounding. How card tips are recorded is Content required from Finance.

    Table

    Refunds and chargebacks

    Money going out of a card or online account on a restaurant's department: a refund to a guest, a chargeback or a fee. Each one is a case to check against the bank or terminal statement.

    Table

    Tender mapping

    Every Simphony tender: what it is and which BC accounts receive its money, and in how many days. The proposal comes from the tender's category and name and the bank accounts seen on the restaurants; save it once it is right.

    Location intelligence Open in the Executive dashboard ›

    One line per restaurant: Simphony location | name | key=value … with brand (the icon), company (BC company), bc (BC location), customer (the BC customer its POS sales post to), dept (its BC department for the P&L, when not the same as bc), area, region (anything here keeps it off the city map), currency (wins over Simphony), map=x,y (position on the city map, % of width and height) and seasonal.     Receivables & payables email

    A daily email with the exceptions of the Payables and Receivables control sections: overdue beyond the critical limit, supplier accounts in debit and concentration, with the ageing; every exception, document by document, comes as an attached PDF. It is sent through the mail server set up in Purchasing → Settings, so no password is entered here.

    Off

    Cost control weekly email

    Every week, for the week before, a short report for the cost controller: highlights against the previous report (stock against the G/L, slow and dead stock, stock received and never used, days of cover, items below zero, recipe coverage, item master issues), an action list with priority, owner and value, and five lines each from Inventory, Movement & dead stock, Typology & turnover, Recipe integrity and Item cards (card checks). Every line behind it comes in an Excel file. Sent through the Purchasing mail server.

    Off

    Negative stock daily email

    Every day, every item below zero at every location at the end of the day before, each line with its likely cause and owner: receipt not posted (Stock manager), recipe wrong (Cost control), sold without purchase (Purchasing). An open purchase order or a transfer shipped and not received is shown as the evidence; otherwise the cause is read from the item ledger since the line went below zero. New lines first, with how many days each has been below zero. One email per company to the three owners (Email recipients by company → Negative stock · daily), one per location to the location's own people; every line in an Excel file. Sent through the Purchasing mail server.

    Off

    Sales blocked by stock daily email

    Every day at the time set, what Sales → Blocked by stock shows, read fresh: the components whose quantity stops the sales from being posted in Business Central now (with the orders, portions and sales held), the ones today's Simphony sales will run out of before they are imported, and the ones BC still flags whose stock has come. The whole report in an Excel file. One email per company (Email recipients by company → Sales blocked by stock · daily: cost control and operations, unless changed there), one per location to the location's own people with that location only. Sent through the Purchasing mail server.

    Off

    SevenRooms daily email

    Every day at the time set, what Sales → SevenRooms ↔ Simphony shows for the last 7 days, read fresh: yesterday's reservations of each restaurant against Simphony (covers seated against the guests, no-shows, the sales that came with a reservation), the cases to correct, the guests rated 1 or 2, and today's and the next days' book with the forecast. Everything in an Excel file. One email per company (Email recipients by company → Reservations against Simphony · daily: the unit managers and operations, unless changed there), one per location to the location's own people with that location only. No guest's name, phone or email is in it. Sent through the Purchasing mail server.

    Off

    Brand performance email

    One email per brand, to the brand's own addresses with finance and operations in Cc. Weekly, for the week before: sales of every location (Simphony, excluding VAT) against the budget, the week before and the same weekdays last year; guests, checks and the average check; sales by day; the month to date with the costs posted so far. Monthly, for the month before, twice: provisional on the first working day and final on the day set below, once payroll and stock usage are posted: the P&L of the brand (sales, food & beverage, labour, prime cost, other costs, EBITDA) against budget and last year, the month and the year to date, every location. Brands and locations come from the registry in Location intelligence. Sent through the Purchasing mail server.

    Off

    To · the addresses of each brand (a brand left blank gets no email)

    Sales weekly email

    Every week (Monday by default), the sales of the week before against last year (the same weekdays) and the budget of those days, with the week before, checks, the average check and the month to date, and the categories (Simphony major groups, family groups in a restaurant's email) against last year and the same weekdays a month before. One email with all the restaurants by brand goes to the people of the companies; each restaurant with people of its own gets one more email with that restaurant only, day by day. Who gets it is set in Email recipients below, under Sales against last year and budget: unit manager, operations manager, head chef, executive chef, COO, CFO, CEO and others, for all companies, one company or one location (a role at a location gets that location's email). Sent through the Purchasing mail server.

    Off

    P&L memo · monthly

    Every month on the day set (the 20th by default, when payroll and stock usage are posted), the P&L of the month before for each company: a memo in sentences (sales, food and beverage, labour, other costs and EBITDA against the budget and last year, the year to date and the forecast, the restaurants ahead and behind, the accounts that moved EBITDA most), the P&L table for the month and the year to date, and every restaurant and department. Who gets it is set in Email recipients below, under P&L memo · monthly (CEO and CFO in To, COO, finance, accounting and management in Cc by default): people set for several companies get them in one email; a restaurant with people of its own gets its own P&L. Sent through the Purchasing mail server.
